summary: SFUSD's Mission Bay School is a four-story TK-5 campus at 1415 Owens St (about 81,800 sq ft per the design team; SF Standard says approximately 80,000) designed by DLR Group and built by McCarthy Building Companies, the design-build team SFUSD hired in 2022, under a reported $95.4 million construction contract funded by SFUSD's 2016 bond program (Proposition A). SFUSD held the ribbon cutting on August 6, 2026 and scheduled the first PreK/TK/K students for August 2026, making it Mission Bay's first public elementary school and SFUSD's first new school in about a decade.

milestones.text: The Board of Supervisors adopts the Mission Bay Redevelopment Plan; a neighborhood elementary school was part of its original vision
SFUSD announces it has hired DLR Group (design architect) and McCarthy Building Companies (design-build contractor)
Official groundbreaking ceremony, attended by the project team, students, children and Mayor London Breed
SFUSD's October 2025 announcement scheduled construction to be completed by January 2026; no completion report was found
First students (Pre-K, TK, combined TK-K special ed, and Kindergarten) begin attending under Principal Monette Benitez
School is planned to grow one grade at a time into a full TK-5 (with Preschool) campus by 2032
OTC alterations permit 202408027795 issued for installation of a new fire water line from Owens Street to the new building
OCII Commission Chair Scott reports having attended a ribbon-cutting event at the Mission Bay grade school near Chase Center, at which children took part

costs.what: Construction contract for the school, reported as $95.4 million at the August 2026 opening
Total project cost cited at the August 2026 opening (broader than the McCarthy construction contract; likely includes design, site work, FF&E and soft costs, not itemized in the source)
Revised cost on OTC alterations permit 202408027795 for installation of a new fire water line from Owens Street to the new building at 1415 Owens St
OTC alterations permit 202412056214 to revise the fire department connection from a 2-way to a 4-way detail at 1415 Owens St (estimated and revised cost)

facts.value: 1415 Owens St (site bounded by Owen Street, Nelson Rising Lane, Mission Bay Boulevard and 6th Street)
SFUSD's 2016 Proposition A school facilities bond (voter-approved)
Reported inconsistently: 'more than 400 students' at full build-out (2026 report) vs. 'up to 550' and '600' in 2022 pre-construction reporting -- not reconciled, see open questions

Designed to be twice as sustainable as SFUSD's standard; Universal Design for Learning with movable glass partitions joining classrooms; ground-floor spaces with direct outdoor access; built-in classroom observation rooms for teacher training on each floor

A 'Mission Bay Hub' STEM program serving high schoolers from six SF high schools (SF Standard); described in 2022 as a STEM-focused linked learning hub preparing students for careers in health, bioscience and STEM fields, plus district professional-development space

open_questions: Full-build-out (2032) enrollment capacity is not consistently reported across sources ('more than 400', 'up to 550', '600'); no SFUSD primary-source capacity figure was found.

Total project cost is ambiguous: SFUSD's construction contract with McCarthy was $95.39M, but a trade-press piece at the 2026 opening cites $129M as the project total, with no breakdown of the difference found.
No SFUSD document names a square-footage figure officially; the 81,800/82,000 sq ft figures come from trade press, not the district itself.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.

CORRECTED 2026-09-24: the 2032-08 grade-growth milestone (school growing one grade per year to full TK-5) carried `status: "planned"`, which the site's timeline reads as the whole record reverting to pre-construction 'planned' status for any date past August 2032 -- even though the school is already built and open (same bug mechanism reported by a site visitor on 'Prequel Park (Power Station sub-area)', found here by auditing every record for the same pattern). That milestone describes enrollment growth, not a change in construction status, so it should never have carried a status field at all; removed it. The milestone's date, text and sources are unchanged.

2026-09-29: no source was found for a 2022 UCSF transfer of the school site to SFUSD or a 1988 set-aside, so both were removed; no post-completion report was found for the January 2026 construction-completion schedule; the exact first day of school (Aug 17, 2026 per a SF Chronicle article that could not be fetched) is not confirmed from a readable source.
